preconditions: Explicit diagnostic iterator and a fresh external private spool directory; all protected project/input/output roots are supplied as trusted boundaries. Current native POSIX descriptor operations only.
steps: Compare the complete stable diagnostic sequence across tiny batches and pages, including duplicates, mandatory errors, large individual records, large integer coordinates and an empty source.
Generate a real run larger than 4 MiB with a one-pass iterator and 32-KiB encoded batches; measure only the selected Python allocation window.
Verify complete hashed run bindings, monotone record/byte delivery positions, unchanged protected files, short writes and retained partial own files on a labelled I/O failure.
Reject linked, overlapping, replaced, changed or non-private storage without returning the affected page or claiming completion.

oracle.requirement_contract: Jede potenziell große Verarbeitungsphase MUSS einen dokumentierten granularen Fortschritts- und Fortsetzungsvertrag nach Anhang P.5 besitzen.
oracle.scope: 6.f.W: hashed JSONL batch runs and pairwise stable merging preserve every Diagnostic and its existing ordering, independently of the soft encoded batch target. The complete final run is delivered through a monotone record/byte cursor with full hash and descriptor guards; prefixes are not complete results. Oversized individual diagnostics make real progress. Owned private files lie outside declared protected roots, survive failures and are never automatically deleted. The cursor explicitly declares durable_checkpoint=false; construction, merge and cross-process resume remain a partial P.5 scope.

open_items: Only explicit external diagnostic sorting and a live in-process delivery cursor are implemented. Persistent Work generations, portable resume/source snapshot bindings, pausable merge cursors, automatic root selection, locks and all-command integration remain open. Intermediate runs are retained, so disk use can grow with merge levels. The graph/frontier/all-shortest-path requirement SR-REQ-0585 remains open; no graph behavior is inferred from this diagnostic test suite. No total RSS, host quota or cross-platform completion is claimed.
